editorNote: The calendar turns with computers on the front-page of the national conversation: bargain micros, console games, and office PCs all crowd the same holiday counter.
morningLine: New Year shoppers are comparing game cartridges, budget BASIC machines, and serious office systems in the same electronics aisles.

lead.headline: New Year Counters Sell Computers as Machine of the Year
lead.summary: TIME's Jan. 3 issue crowns the computer as Machine of the Year just as holiday buyers weigh the Timex Sinclair 1000, VIC-20, Commodore 64, IBM PC, Atari consoles, and game cartridges as mainstream gifts rather than specialist curiosities.
lead.confidence: High for TIME issue date and hardware guide; week framing is anchored to the Dec. 27-Jan. 2 issue window and holiday retail context.

computerItems.title: TIME turns the annual spotlight from a person to a machine
computerItems.summary: The Jan. 3, 1983 Jan. 3 issue package treats the computer as the defining force of 1982, emphasizing its spread through homes, schools, and offices.

computerItems.title: Atari shock still hangs over game makers
computerItems.summary: Trade front-pageage in early January points back to Atari lowering expectations in December and to Imagic delaying a stock offering, a warning sign beneath strong cartridge sales.
computerItems.confidence: Medium; reported shortly after this week and tied to late-1982 events.

computerItems.title: Budget computers pull first-time buyers toward BASIC
computerItems.summary: TIME lists the Timex Sinclair 1000 at $99 and the VIC-20 at $299, showing how low-cost machines are being sold as entry points for programming and games.
computerItems.confidence: High for model and list-price context.

computerItems.title: Arcade hits keep shaping home wish lists
computerItems.summary: Pac-Man, River Raid, Donkey Kong, and other arcade-derived names remain the language shoppers use when comparing cartridges and consoles.
computerItems.confidence: Medium; product availability verified, exact store ranking varies by market.

market.headline: Hardware aisles widen while game stocks wobble

bbsNote: Local modem culture remains a hobbyist lane: owners trade tips, public-domain BASIC programs, and game hints over slow dial-up connections.
curiosity: For the first time, TIME selected a non-human Machine of the Year, making the personal computer a year-end newsstand symbol.

briefs.title: Tootsie wins New Year weekend

briefs.title: The Dark Crystal holds holiday fantasy crowds

briefs.title: E.T. still refuses to leave theaters
briefs.summary: E.T. remains in the weekend top ten after 30 weeks, with a domestic total above $317 million by Jan. 2.
